To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the comparison of the genomic sequence of the phytopathogenic H. rubisubalbicans and endophytic H. seropediae SmR1 by suppressive subtraction hybridization, in silico analysis and knockout of the cellulose biosynthesis gene, wssD, in H. seroepediae SmR, revealed that the production of cellulose is involved in the maize root surface attachment by H. rubriubalbicans.
the genomic differences between Herbaspirillum species revealed by SSH suggested the involvement of LPS and adhesins in the contrasting phenotypic behavior of these organisms.

the genomic comparison of Herbaspirillum species by suppressive subtracting hybridization (SSH), partial genome sequencing and in silico comparison, revealed that the production of cellulose and adhesins might be responsible for the contrasting phenotype between H. seropedaicae SmRl and H. rubisubalbicans.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes involved in endophytic colonization and the pathogenic life style of the Herbaspirillum genus.
the identification of genomic and transcriptomic features that are potentially associated with the contrasting phenotypic behavior of these two closely related species.
the identification of genes involved in the contrasting behavior of the two closely related Herbaspirillum spp. and the role of these genes in their phenotypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the genomic differences between H. rubristubalbicans and H. seropediae may be responsible for the contrasting phenotypes.
the phenotypes of the two species are determined by a complex combination of genomic differences, including the presence/absence of genes, and their differential regulation.
H. rubisubalbicans is a pathogen of sugar cane, whereas H. seropediae is an endophyte.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phenotypic differences between these two species could be attributed to a few genomic differences, and these genomic differences could be the result of the different ecological niches of these two closely related bacteria.
the genomic differences revealed by SSH between H. rubisubalbicans and H. seropedaicae are related to the contrasting phenotypes of these two organisms.
the phenotypes of the two Herbaspirillum species could be explained by the differences found in their genomic sequence.
The main takeaway from our work is that
H. rubrissubalbicans is capable of producing cellulose, and the production of cellulose is a potential factor for the attachment to the maize root surface and endophytic association.
H. rubrissubalbicans and H. seropediae are closely related but have distinct genomic and phenotypic features that are responsible for the different phenotypes of these organisms.
a comparison of the genomes and phenotypic characteristics between closely related species is a powerful tool to identify molecular determinants of contrasting phenotypic behavior.
